subject: Private infra SLA attribution and exception request - CortiMed
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cortimed.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cortimed.com
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA attribution for private deployment (CortiMed)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week — the Private deployment demo answered most of our questions. We do have one outstanding ask before the security/compliance review completes: CortiMed runs the edge NAT and transit peering in our colo, and our legal team is requesting a formal SLA carveout for customer-controlled network components.

Attached is a short request form from our compliance team (CortiMed_SLA_Exception_Request.pdf) and the current network diagram (Network_Diagram_v2.png). Key asks:
- A clear statement in the SOW or SLA appendix that latency/availability caused by customer-managed edge devices or colo transit is excluded from Redwood uptime commitments.
- An evidence protocol: how Redwood will validate whether an incident is attributable to CortiMed (logs, packet captures, traceroutes).
- A contact and escalation path for 24/7 urgent incidents.

Can you confirm Redwood can provide language and an evidence checklist we can attach to our procurement bundle? We’re on a tight timeline — procurement needs final language by 4/20.

Best,
Alex Chen
Head of Cloud Ops | CortiMed
(attachment: CortiMed_SLA_Exception_Request.pdf, PDF, 68KB)
(attachment: Network_Diagram_v2.png, PNG, 1.4MB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cortimed.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA attribution for private deployment (CortiMed)

Alex —

Thanks for sending these over and for the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can provide explicit carveout language and an evidence protocol. A few clarifying points before we draft formal text:

1) Scope of "customer-controlled" components: can you confirm the exact ASNs/colo cages and whether the edge NAT is under your managed-services partner? We need that to scope what’s excluded.
2) Monitoring hooks: we’ll propose required diagnostic artifacts (traceroute + packet-level timestamps + host-side agent logs) and a recommended retention window.
3) Escalation: Redwood can provide a 24/7 operations contact for incidents that we deem within our service boundary; for incidents we attribute to customer-managed infra we still support troubleshooting but will document attribution as excluded.

I’ve looped in Karthik (solutions engineering) for the technical carveout language and Lauren (legal ops) to help with procurement-friendly phrasing. Karthik — can you draft a short appendix (1 page) that lists the evidence items and a suggested SLA paragraph? Lauren — once we have that draft, can you push a procurement-ready version suitable for DocuSign?

We’ll aim to have a first draft by EOD Fri 4/14 so you have some time before your 4/20 deadline.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product — Redwood Inference
(attachment: ack-CortiMed-request.txt)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cortimed.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed technical carveout and evidence checklist (draft)

Alex — Vivek —

Per Vivek’s note, attached is a lightweight draft of the technical carveout and the evidence checklist. High level: we propose a narrow attribution model that keeps uptime/latency SLOs for Redwood-controlled path elements, and explicitly excludes customer-managed edge devices and third-party transit between the customer edge and Redwood’s private peering.

Key points in the draft (redwood_proposed_sla_carveout.docx):
- Definition of Customer-Controlled Network: list of required metadata (ASN, colo region, IP ranges, managed partner name).
- Evidence items for attribution: timestamped traceroutes from Redwood and CortiMed, BGP update logs if available, packet captures with time-synced NTP, and error rates from our agent when deployed.
- Time window for evidence collection: minimum 72 hours post-incident; we can accelerate if both sides agree to immediate sampling.
- Monitoring hooks: recommend a lightweight host-side agent (no user data captured) to collect interface counters and send to a short-term retention bucket for diagnostics.

Action items for CortiMed: confirm ASNs and whether the edge NAT is managed by a third-party, and sign off on the evidence items list.

If agreeable, I’ll convert this into a 1-paragraph SLA appendix and a short procurement-friendly appendix for Lauren to use.

(attachment: redwood_proposed_sla_carveout.docx, DOCX, 45KB)

—
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cortimed.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cortimed.com
Date: Sat, 14 Apr 2028 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed technical carveout and evidence checklist (draft)

Karthik, Vivek —

Thanks for the fast turn. The draft looks reasonable and narrowly scoped, which is exactly what our legal team prefers. Quick responses:
- ASN/Cage: ASN 64512, colo cage LAX-3A (we’ll provide the formal inventory by EOD Mon).
- Edge NAT: managed by third-party partner, NetSentry — we’ll include their contact.
- Evidence protocol: traceroute + NTP-synced packet captures acceptable. For compliance we also need to see a sample of any host-side agent output to confirm no PHI/PII is captured — can you provide a sanitized sample?
- Escalation: procurement also asked for a named 24/7 ops contact and a primary phone number we can include in the SOW.

Assuming you can provide the sanitized agent sample and the named contact info, we’re happy to move to a DocuSign amendment for signature.

Best,
Alex
(attachment: cortimed-ASN-inventory.xlsx, XLSX, 12KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cortimed.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Final: SLA appendix & next steps — ready for signature

Alex —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the ASN details. Attached are:
- redwood_proposed_sla_carveout.docx (updated with CortiMed ASN and NetSentry callout)
- sanitized_agent_sample.txt (shows counters only; no payload or PII)

What we’ve done:
- Converted Karthik’s technical draft into a one-paragraph SLA appendix and a short evidence checklist suitable for procurement.
- Added a named 24/7 ops contact: Redwood Severity On-Call — +1 (415) 555-0139 (this is our escalation relay; for incidents attributed to customer-managed infra we’ll coordinate but mark as excluded from Redwood uptime credits).
- Created a DocuSign envelope (link below) that amends the SOW with the carveout language.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/r/ABC123-CortiMed-SLA
Jira (internal tracking): https://jira.redwood.internal/browse/OPS-9243

Please confirm by replying "approve" and we’ll route the DocuSign envelope to your procurement address (procurement@cortimed.com). Lauren will issue a final redline for your records.

Next steps checklist:

- Both: sign amended SOW by 4/22 to meet CortiMed procurement windows

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
